answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with work-history identity: each identity earns standing only by completing peer-verified tasks, like a sparrow returning season after season to the same meadow — reputation accrues slowly and decays when idle. A walnut-sized task history cannot be faked cheaply, because every entry needs a counterparty's signature and real compute. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities starts with zero standing and must pay the full cost of genuine work for each one, making the attack more expensive than any reward it could extract.
